newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE sugar eases in slow post holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE sugar eases in slow post holiday trade.

text.p: LIFFE sugar eased in slow post holiday trade.
"There's not much to report," one trader said. "It's been a long weekend."
By 1008 GMT just 60 lots had been traded, 59 of them on front month August. It was 30 cents lower at $320.40.
Monday was a holiday in Britain, as well as in the United States, which meant that the London and New York markets were closed.
"Paris was open on Monday, but it didn't really set the world alight," he said.
New York futures finished firmer on Friday in thin activity.

In London, no fundamental news moved the market in early Monday trading, traders said. But Turkey's state sugar refinery, Turkseker, is planning to sell about 135,000 tonnes of sugar to be destined to Iran and Iraq by means of local traders at prices of about $15 to $35 per tonne over Paris prices, a senior company official said on Tuesday.
China produced 6.604 million tonnes of sugar in the 1996/97 crushing season (October-April), up by 376,000 tonnes from the last season, an official said on Tuesday.
